newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Firm gasoline gets nod from APIs.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Firm gasoline gets nod from APIs.

text.p: Spot gasoline differentials east of the Rocky Mountains got a nod of confirmation from this week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API), which showed a bullish drop in stocks, traders said.
"The gasoline numbers pretty much confirmed what the cash market has been doing for the last week," he said, referring to sharp gains seen on both the Gulf and New York Harbor.

API said gasoline stocks fell by 3.1 million barrels to 194.6 million, helped by implied demand of 8.59 million barrels per day (bpd) that was spurred by imports that dipped to 264,000 bpd and output that fell to 7.87 million bpd.
Underlying August NYMEX gasoline futures surged nearly a cent on ACCESS over the early settlement of 66.47 cents a gallon, while heat too got a upward shot from
GULF COAST
News of a lightning strike of Exxon's fluid catalytic cracking unit at its Baytown refinery near Houston underpinned much of the strength in gasoline.

But by the end of the day, assessments on prompt "M1" regular conventional southern-grade unleaded grew vague as the deadline for shipping product out of Houston on the Colonial Pipeline expired in a shroud of mystery.
"Tomorrow we won't care, so I don't know if it's ignorance or apathy, said one Houston trader.
But before the deadline, the the bellwether grade went through the roof, trading as high as 2.00 cents over September NYMEX or 1.509 cents firmer than at the start of the day.
Offers for the newly-prompt M1 for delivery on Colonial's back 22nd scheduling cycle were pegged at 1.00 cent over September NYMEX after trading at 0.80 and 0.50 cent over earlier in the day.
Any month M1 barrels were pegged at around 2.850 cents under the September print.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Gasoline differentials jumped higher early Tuesday and held on through late trading, as buyers continued to chase prices higher.
"It's outrageous," one frustrated gasoline buyer said, describing the jump in prompt reformulated A2 differentials to 3.25 cents over the August NYMEX, a gain of about 1.00 cent on the day.

Tightness in MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether), an A2 additive, drove prices higher in recent weeks. Traders put MTBE prices between 1.00 to 1.02 cents a gallon, slightly off its top of 1.03 cents seen last week.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline rallied even higher, finishing the day between 2.25 and 2.00 cents under the August futures, a gain 1.50 cents from Monday.
Traders also pointed to market rumors that Tosco would idle its 140,000 barrel-a-day catalytic cracker at its Bayway, New Jersey refinery as a bullish factor.

However, Tosco refused to detail the maintenance at the refinery, though earlier a Tosco official has said a crude unit at the facility would be shut for a period of weeks starting at the end of July.
MIDCONTINENT
Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials weakened slightly in quiet trade amid the sharp rise in NYMEX gasoline futures and little demand.

Prompt Group Three barrels edged down a quarter cent to 1.75/1.50 cents below the print after falling more than a penny at midday. Due to the deep spread between August and September futures, Group Three early August barrels were pegged at 2.00/2.50 cents over the September screen.
"The Merc is higher and there is no demand," said a Group Three player.
Chicago material held steady, finding a floor in the strong values in the U.S. Gulf. Chicago unleaded held at 3.00/3.25 cents for prompt August barrels, with the any months at 1.50/1.75 cents.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1620
